questions.questionHtml: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana was started during the _________.
questions.solution: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Yojana was started during the Eighth Five Year Plan, which was from 1992-1997. The aim of the scheme was to provide employment opportunities to the unemployed youth of the country by promoting self-employment and entrepreneurship.

questions.question: In which state is the Maski inscription located at present?
questions.questionHtml: In which state is the Maski inscription located at present?
questions.solution: The Maski inscription is an important archaeological discovery as it is one of the earliest known examples of Brahmi script, dating back to the 3rd century BCE. The inscription was discovered in 1915 by a British archaeologist named F.E. Keay during his excavations in Maski, Karnataka.

questions.question: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?
questions.questionHtml: When did the Drafting Committee publish the first draft of the Indian Constitution?

questions.question: Asad Ali Khan is best known for his mastery over which of the given musical instruments?
questions.questionHtml: Asad Ali Khan is best known for his mastery over which of the given musical instruments?
questions.solution: Asad Ali Khan is best known for his mastery over the Rudra Veena, which is a stringed musical instrument. The Rudra Veena is a rare and ancient instrument that has been in existence for over 2000 years and is known for its deep and meditative sound.

questions.question: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and __________ rivers is known as Kumaon Himalayas.
questions.questionHtml: The part of the Himalayas lying between Satluj and __________ rivers is known as Kumaon Himalayas.
questions.solution: The Kumaon Himalayas lie between the Satluj river in the west and the Kali river in the east. The Kali river forms the boundary between India and Nepal.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations is credited with writing literary pieces for the abolition of Sati Pratha?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following organisations is credited with writing literary pieces for the abolition of Sati Pratha?
questions.solution: The Brahmo Samaj is credited with writing literary pieces for the abolition of Sati Pratha. Sati Pratha was a practice where a widow was expected to immolate herself on her husband's funeral pyre.

questions.question: The pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon ___________.
questions.questionHtml: The pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon ___________.
questions.solution: The Consolidated Fund of India is the main fund of the government and all revenues received by the government, loans raised by the government, and money received in repayment of loans form part of this fund. The pensions payable to or in respect of the officers and servants of the Supreme Court are charged upon the Consolidated Fund of India, which means that the funds for their pensions come from this main fund of the government.

questions.question: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
questions.questionHtml: On 20 July 2021, the Supreme Court struck down certain provisions of part IX B of the Constitution of India. Part IX B was related to:
questions.solution: The correct answer is Co-operative Societies. Part IX B of the Constitution of India deals with the provisions related to the formation and functioning of cooperative societies. The Supreme Court has struck down specific provisions of Part IX B, which means that some of the rules related to cooperative societies are no longer valid.

questions.question: which of the following Indian states was the host of the 36 th national games?
questions.questionHtml: which of the following Indian states was the host of the 36<sup>th</sup> national games?
questions.solution: The correct answer is Gujarat, which hosted the 36th National Games in 2016. The National Games is a biennial multi-sport event in India, where athletes from different states compete against each other. The first National Games were held in 1924 in Delhi, and since then, it has been held in various states across India.

questions.question: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?
questions.questionHtml: Which element of Group 17 has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu with average abundance of 75.77% and 24.23%, respectively?
questions.solution: Chlorine is the element of Group 17 that has two isotopes of masses 35 and 37 amu. The average abundance of the isotopes is 75.77% for 35 amu and 24.23% for 37 amu. Chlorine has the atomic number 17 and its chemical symbol is Cl.

questions.question: ‘Dalkhai’ is a folk dance of which of the following states of India?
questions.questionHtml: ‘Dalkhai’ is a folk dance of which of the following states of India?
questions.solution: Dalkhai is a popular folk dance of the state of Odisha in India, especially in the western parts of the state. The dance is usually performed by young girls and women during the festival of Dussehra and is accompanied by traditional musical instruments like the dhol, nagara, and harmonium.

questions.question: Which of the following countries never hosted the Paralympic games ?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following countries never hosted the Paralympic games ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is India. India has never hosted the Paralympic games. The Paralympic games are an international multi-sport event for athletes with disabilities. It is held every four years, following the Olympic games. The first Paralympic games were held in Rome, Italy in 1960

questions.question: There are 3 members in a family. The average age of the father and mother is 40 years. The average age of the father, mother and daughter is 30 years. Find the age (in years) of the daughter.
questions.questionHtml: There are 3 members in a family. The average age of the father and mother is 40 years. The average age of the father, mother and daughter is 30 years. Find the age (in years) of the daughter.
questions.solution:
Total age of father and mother = 40 × 2 = 80 years

Total age of father, mother and daughter = 90

So the age daughter = 90 – 80 = 10 years

Gain = Total profit ( i.e., profit from selling + profit from the false weight)/actual CP

Actual Profit percent = (35/80) × 100 ⇒ 43.75%

questions.question: Find the smallest number that can be subtracted from 148109326 so that it becomes divisible by 8.
questions.questionHtml: Find the smallest number that can be subtracted from 148109326 so that it becomes divisible by 8.
questions.solution:
Divisibility rule of 8: When the number made by the last 3 digits of a number is divisible by 8 then the number is also divisible by 8.

Apart from this if the last three or more digits of a number are zero then the number is divisible by 8.

The last 3 digits are 326 and so, for it to be completely divisible by 8 we have to deduct 6 from the given number.

questions.question: A policeman noticed a thief from 300 m. The thief started running and the policeman was chasing him. The thief and the policeman ran at the speeds of 8 km/h and 9 km/h, respectively. What was the distance between them after 3 minutes?
questions.questionHtml: A policeman noticed a thief from 300 m. The thief started running and the policeman was chasing him. The thief and the policeman ran at the speeds of 8 km/h and 9 km/h, respectively. What was the distance between them after 3 minutes?
questions.solution:
Distance between policeman and thief in starting = 300 m

Relative speed of policeman and thief, if same directions = (9 – 8) = 1 × (5/18) = (5/18) m/sec

Distance covered in 180 seconds = (5/18) × 180 = 50 m

Distance between them after 180 seconds= 300 – 50 = 250 m

y + 2x - [y - (y - x + y) - (x + y) + y] - 2y.
questions.solution:
Given:

y + 2x - [y - (y - x + y) - (x + y) + y] - 2y

Concept used:

Follow the BODMAS rule according to the table given below:

Calculation:

y + 2x - [y - (y - x + y) - (x + y) + y] - 2y

⇒ y + 2x - [y - y + x - y - x - y + y] - 2y

questions.question: A, B and C, working alone, can complete a job in 16, 24 and 36 days, respectively. In how many days can they complete the job if they work together?

questions.solution:
Using the LCM method,

The LCM of 16, 24 and 36 = 144(total work)

A's efficiency = 144/16 ⇒ 9

B's efficiency = 144/24 ⇒ 6

C's efficiency = 144/36 ⇒ 4

Time = 144 / 19 ⇒ 7 (11/19)

questions.question: Rakshit, Ajay, and Satish are sanitation workers in a Municipal Corporation. Rakshit alone takes 20 hours to clean a drain while Ajay takes 12 hours when working alone to do the same. All three together take only 5 hours to clean the drain. In how many hours, can Satish complete the work alone?
questions.questionHtml: Rakshit, Ajay, and Satish are sanitation workers in a Municipal Corporation. Rakshit alone takes 20 hours to clean a drain while Ajay takes 12 hours when working alone to do the same. All three together take only 5 hours to clean the drain. In how many hours, can Satish complete the work alone?
questions.solution:
Alternate Method Suppose total work is 60 units (LCM of 5, 12 and 20)

Efficiency of all three = 60 / 5 = 12

Efficiency of Rakshit = 60 / 20 = 3

Efficiency of Ajay = 60 / 12 = 5

Efficiency of Satish = (12 - 8) = 4

Number of days taken by Satish alone to finish the work = 60 / 4 = 15 days

questions.question: 15 men and 25 women can complete a piece of work in 9.6 days. If 16 women can complete the same work in 27 days, find the number of days in which 16 men can complete the same work.
questions.questionHtml: 15 men and 25 women can complete a piece of work in 9.6 days. If 16 women can complete the same work in 27 days, find the number of days in which 16 men can complete the same work.
questions.solution:
According to the question,

⇒ (15M + 25W) × 3.2 = 16W × 9

⇒ 15M + 25W = 45W

⇒ 15M = 20W

Time taken to complete the total work by 16 men =

questions.question: A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article: i. Two successive discounts of 15% each ii. A discount of 25% followed by a discount of 5% iii. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10% iv. A discount of 30% Under which scheme will the selling price be maximum?
questions.questionHtml:
A shopkeeper offers the following discount schemes for buyers on an article:

i. Two successive discounts of 15% each

ii. A discount of 25% followed by a discount of 5%

iii. Two successive discounts of 20% and 10%

iv. A discount of 30%

Under which scheme will the selling price be maximum?
questions.solution:
Calculation:

M.P - face value

S.P – Selling Price

Plan I

Effective discount = 15 + 15 - (152/100)

⇒ 30 – 2.25 = 27.75%

M.P : S.P = 100 : 72.25

Scheme II:

Effective discount = 25 + 5 – (25 × 5)/100

⇒ 30 – 1.25 = 28.75%

M.P : S.P = 100 : 71.25

Scheme III:

Effective discount = 20 + 10 – (20 × 10)/100

⇒ 30 – 2 = 28%

M.P : S.P = 100 : 72

Scheme IV:

discount 30%

M.P : S.P = 100 : 70

As in scheme i we get the least discount, so the selling price in scheme i is the maximum. Hence the correct option is 4.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Come". 

 Key Points

  • The phrase "(3) alive" requires a verb that will indicate the learning material becomes or appears alive to the students.
  • "Come alive" is a commonly used idiomatic expression that means to become energized or exciting.
  • In pedagogical context, "come alive" means making study material more interesting, engaging, and memorable.
  • In this context, "come" is the most appropriate word to use.
  • The phrase "come alive" implies that the props such as notes, handouts, or slides used by the teacher will invigorate the learning material, making it more engaging and memorable for the students.
  • So, the sentence should read: "So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts, and slides that will make the learning material come alive for the students and stay that way with them."

Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 4". 

Additional Information

  • "Stay alive" might seem appropriate at first, but it is typically used to denote survival, not transformation into a livelier state.
  • "Depart alive" doesn't make sense because "depart" means to leave, which connotes movement away, not transformation or enhancement.
  • "Go alive" also doesn't fit well because "go" conveys movement from one place to another rather than transformation.

  • Realise (समझना) means to become fully aware of (something) as a fact; understand clearly.
    • Example: He did not realise the gravity of the situation until it was too late.
  • Realise in the context of the passage implies becoming aware or acknowledging something important - in this case, that complicated sentences can be difficult for students to understand.
  • Hence, the correct answer is realise.
Therefore, the correct answer is “Option 3”.
 
Additional Information
  • Guess (मान लेना) means to estimate or suppose (something) without sufficient information to be sure of being correct.
  • Detect (पता लगाना) means to discover or identify the presence of something concealed.
  • Decide (निर्णय लेना) means to make a choice from a number of alternatives.
